pl-l4d10c2-d1e115.summary: States that these and similar objections come from those who follow the law of nature in a divine mystery, whose unbelief the following testimonies refute.
claims: Natural law does not govern the divine mystery.

pl-l4d10c2-d1e118.summary: Cites Christ: 'take, this is my body'.
claims: Christ declared the bread his body.

pl-l4d10c2-d1e121.summary: Quotes Ambrose: if Elijah's word could bring fire from heaven, will not Christ's word change substances? Of the whole world's works it is written 'he spoke and they were made'; the word that could make from nothing what was not, cannot it change what is into what it was not? It is no less to give new natures to things than to change them.
claims: Christ's word can change substances.
The word that created from nothing can change what exists.

pl-l4d10c2-d1e131.summary: Adds Ambrose: if we seek the natural order, a woman conceives with a man; the Virgin conceived beyond nature, and the body we make is from the Virgin. Why seek the order of nature in Christ's body, when his birth from the Virgin was beyond nature?
claims: The virgin birth shows Christ's body is beyond natural order.

pl-l4d10c2-d1e137.summary: Adds Ambrose: before the blessing another species is named; after consecration the body is signified; before it is called something else, after it blood. You say 'Amen', that is, it is true; let the heart feel what the word says.
claims: After consecration it is Christ's body and blood.

pl-l4d10c2-d1e143.summary: Quotes Augustine: in the species of bread and wine we see, we honor invisible things, flesh and blood, and do not weigh these species as before consecration, since we confess that before it there is bread and wine formed by nature, after it Christ's flesh and blood consecrated by the blessing.
claims: Before consecration bread and wine; after it Christ's flesh and blood.

pl-l4d10c2-d1e152.summary: Adds Ambrose: bread is ordinary on the altar before the sacred words; when consecration comes, the bread becomes Christ's flesh, by consecration made by Christ's word.
claims: Consecration by Christ's word makes bread his flesh.

pl-l4d10c2-d1e161.summary: Adds Ambrose: if the Lord's word is so powerful that things began to be which were not, how much more that things which were be changed into something else; so what was bread before consecration is Christ's body after, since his word changes the creature, and wine with water becomes his blood.
claims: The power that creates can more easily change.
Christ's word changes the creature.

pl-l4d10c2-d1e167.summary: Quotes Augustine: as true flesh was created by the Spirit without intercourse, so by the same Spirit Christ's body is made from the substance of bread and wine, and is both truth and figure: truth, as Christ's body and blood are made by the Spirit's power from the substance of bread and wine; figure, what is perceived outwardly.
claims: Christ's body is made from bread and wine by the Spirit.
The eucharist is both truth and figure.

pl-l4d10c2-d1e177.summary: Quotes Eusebius of Emesa: the invisible priest by his word changes visible creatures into the substance of his body and blood by secret power.
claims: Christ, the invisible priest, converts the elements.

pl-l4d10c2-d1e183.summary: Concludes that Christ's true body and blood are on the altar, indeed the whole Christ under each species, and the substance of bread is converted into the body and the substance of wine into the blood.
claims: Christ's true body and blood are on the altar.
The whole Christ is under each species.
The substances of bread and wine are converted into body and blood.

pl-l4d10c2.summary: Refutes with authorities those who follow the law of nature in a divine mystery. Christ: 'this is my body'. Ambrose: if Elijah's word could bring fire from heaven, can Christ's word not change substances? The word that made things from nothing can change what exists; the Virgin's birth was beyond nature; before consecration it is called one thing, after it the body and blood; Christ's word changes the creature. Augustine: after consecration it is Christ's flesh and blood that we honor in the species; as true flesh was created by the Spirit without intercourse, so by the Spirit Christ's body is made from bread and wine, truth within and figure without. Eusebius: the invisible priest changes visible creatures into his body and blood by his word. So Christ's true body and blood, indeed the whole Christ under each species, are on the altar, and the substance of bread and wine is converted into them.
claims: The words of institution affirm the true body.
Christ's word, which created from nothing, can change substances.
The virgin birth shows Christ's body is not bound by nature.
After consecration bread and wine are Christ's body and blood.
The whole Christ is under each species, and the substances of bread and wine are converted.
